# Multi-Stage Dockerfile for Node.js TypeScript Application

## Project Structure
```
project/
├── Dockerfile
├── .dockerignore
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── src/
    └── index.ts
```

---

## Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# ============================================================
# Stage 1: Dependencies
# Install ALL dependencies (including devDependencies)
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS dependencies

# Install dumb-init for proper signal handling in containers
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker layer caching.
# These layers are only invalidated when package files change,
# not when source code changes.
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install ALL dependencies (dev + prod) needed for TypeScript compilation.
# --frozen-lockfile ensures reproducible builds by failing if lock file
# doesn't match package.json, preventing silent dependency drift.
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile


# ============================================================
# Stage 2: Builder
# Compile TypeScript source code
# ============================================================
FROM dependencies AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy compiled dependencies from the previous stage
COPY --from=dependencies /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# Copy TypeScript config and source files
COPY tsconfig.json ./
COPY src/ ./src/

# Compile TypeScript to JavaScript.
# Output goes to /app/dist (as configured in tsconfig.json)
RUN npm run build

# Remove devDependencies after compilation — we only need
# production dependencies in the final image.
# --omit=dev is the modern replacement for --only=production
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile --omit=dev


# ============================================================
# Stage 3: Production (Final Image)
# Contains ONLY what's needed to run the app
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS production

# Security: Install dumb-init to handle PID 1 responsibilities
# (signal forwarding, zombie reaping) properly.
# Without it, Node.js runs as PID 1 and may not handle SIGTERM correctly.
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

# Security: Create a non-root user and group to run the application.
# Running as root in a container is a significant security risk.
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodegroup && \
    adduser -u 1001 -S nodeuser -G nodegroup

WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the production node_modules (no devDependencies)
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodeuser:nodegroup /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# Copy compiled JavaScript from the builder stage
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodeuser:nodegroup /app/dist ./dist

# Copy package.json for runtime metadata (version, scripts, etc.)
COPY --chown=nodeuser:nodegroup package.json ./

# Switch to non-root user BEFORE the final CMD/ENTRYPOINT
USER nodeuser

# Set NODE_ENV to production:
# - Enables production optimizations in many frameworks (e.g., Express)
# - Disables verbose logging/debugging
# - Some packages behave differently (e.g., fewer error details exposed)
ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Document the port the app listens on (informational — does not publish it)
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check: Docker will periodically verify the app is running.
# --interval: how often to run the check
# --timeout:  how long to wait for a response
# --start-period: grace period after container starts
# --retries:  consecutive failures needed to mark as unhealthy
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000/health', (r) => { process.exit(r.statusCode === 200 ? 0 : 1) })" \
    || exit 1

# Use dumb-init as the entrypoint to properly handle OS signals.
# node is then a child process of dumb-init, which correctly forwards
# SIGTERM (used by Docker/Kubernetes for graceful shutdown).
ENTRYPOINT ["dumb-init", "--"]

# Run the compiled application
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

---

## .dockerignore

```dockerignore
# Exclude local node_modules — Docker installs its own inside the image
node_modules/

# Exclude TypeScript source — the final image only needs compiled JS
src/

# Exclude compiled output from local machine — built fresh inside Docker
dist/

# Exclude test files — not needed at runtime
**/*.test.ts
**/*.spec.ts
__tests__/
coverage/

# Exclude development/config files
.git/
.gitignore
.eslintrc*
.prettierrc*
jest.config.*
*.md

# Exclude local environment files — secrets must not be baked into images
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

# Exclude Docker files themselves
Dockerfile*
docker-compose*
.dockerignore

# Exclude OS artifacts
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
```

---

## Supporting Configuration Files

### tsconfig.json
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "commonjs",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": false,
    "sourceMap": false
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.test.ts", "**/*.spec.ts"]
}
```

### package.json
```json
{
  "name": "my-ts-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc --project tsconfig.json",
    "start": "node dist/index.js",
    "dev": "ts-node src/index.ts",
    "lint": "eslint src/**/*.ts",
    "test": "jest"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/express": "^4.17.21",
    "@types/node": "^20.0.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.0"
  }
}
```

### src/index.ts (Example App)
```typescript
import express, { Request, Response } from 'express';

const app = express();
const PORT = process.env.PORT || 3000;

app.use(express.json());

// Health check endpoint — used by Docker HEALTHCHECK
app.get('/health', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  res.status(200).json({ status: 'ok', uptime: process.uptime() });
});

app.get('/', (_req: Request, res: Response) => {
  res.json({ message: 'Hello from TypeScript!' });
});

// Graceful shutdown: handle SIGTERM from Docker/Kubernetes
const server = app.listen(PORT, () => {
  console.log(`Server running on port ${PORT}`);
});

process.on('SIGTERM', () => {
  console.log('SIGTERM received, shutting down gracefully...');
  server.close(() => {
    console.log('Process terminated.');
    process.exit(0);
  });
});
```

## Build & Run Commands

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t my-ts-app:latest .

# Run in production mode
docker run -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env my-ts-app:latest

# Check the final image size
docker images my-ts-app

# Inspect the build layers
docker history my-ts-app:latest

# Run with docker-compose (if applicable)
docker compose up --build
```

---

## Why This Approach Minimizes Image Size

| Decision | Reason |
|---|---|
| `node:20-alpine` base | Alpine Linux is ~5MB vs ~150MB for Debian-based images |
| Multi-stage build | `devDependencies` and `.ts` source files never reach final image |
| `npm ci --omit=dev` in builder | Strips TypeScript compiler, type defs, etc. from production image |
| `.dockerignore` | Prevents `node_modules/` and `src/` from being sent to the build context |
| Non-root user | Security hardening with zero size overhead |
| `dumb-init` | Proper signal handling; the Alpine package is only ~50KB |
| `sourceMap: false` in tsconfig | Excludes `.map` files from `dist/`, reducing copied output |
